Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

advantage noun

a good point, a benefit

also advantages, benefit, benefits, upside, pros and cons, advantages and disadvantages, what’s the advantage?

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.335: commoda pācis … itemque incommoda contrāriōrum
Cic. Tusc. 1.30: orbātōs vītae commodīs

commodum, commodī n.

noun, second declension

advantage, a good point; the good one gets from a thing

Lewis & Short: “advantage, profit (very freq. in all periods)”. A thing’s advantages and drawbacks are its commoda et incommoda; for a drawback alone see problem (incommodum). Also convenience: cum erit tuum commodum, when it suits you (Cic. Att. 12.28.3, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ūtilitās, ūtilitātis f. — usefulness, advantage; in the plural, the benefits of a thing

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 32: sīc et ūtilitātēs ex amīcitiā maximae capientur

    What a thing is good for; in Cicero’s ethics the useful, as against the honourable.

  • prōdest — it is an advantage, it does good

    verb: third person of prōsum, with the dative of the person; what helps is the subject (a noun or an infinitive) · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.64: multum prōdest ea, quae metuuntur, ipsa contemnere; Traupman 92: to be of advantage, prōsum

    “The advantage of X is …” is often turned with the verb: quid prōdest?, what is the advantage? See benefit.

Examples

  • quī ūtilitātem dēfendet, ēnumerābit commoda pācis, opum, potentiae, vectīgālium … itemque incommoda contrāriōrum

    whoever argues for advantage will list the advantages of peace, wealth, power and revenue … and likewise the disadvantages of their oppositesCic. de Or. 2.335

  • multum prōdest ea, quae metuuntur, ipsa contemnere

    there is great advantage in despising the very things that are fearedCic. Tusc. 4.64

See also benefit, advantage, interest, problem.
